title: E flat versus B flat cornet in the Eureka
summary: With the Eureka they used B flat solo cornet, not E flat.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: It's not a horn. Do you have any funeral questions you want to ask? Maybe I have any particular. Who would take the solos, uh, on a funeral march when you were playing with the Eureka? Yeah. And the solo cornet player? Mm-hmm. Would that be the E flat or the B flat? Oh, they didn't use no E flat. Oh, they didn't? Nothing but the B flat. They just wouldn't go E flat. Mm-hmm.
I haven't seen no band with E flat since I left home. Since that bass band at home had that E flat. Mm-hmm. They all used B, voice solo, voice cornet.
